questions.question: What is the key difference between a product 'feature' and a customer 'benefit'?

options.text: Features describe what the product does; benefits describe the value the customer gains
Benefits are technical specifications; features are marketing slogans
They are identical — every feature is automatically a benefit
Features are more important than benefits in customer purchase decisions

questions.explanation: Features are product attributes (e.g., '5000 mAh battery'); benefits are what those features mean to the customer (e.g., 'never run out of power during a long day'). Customers buy benefits, not features.

questions.question: In the traditional Stage-Gate new product development process, what happens at a 'gate'?

options.text: The product is automatically approved for launch
A review decision is made whether to proceed, revise, or terminate the project
The engineering team begins coding without any review
Customer feedback is collected for the first time

questions.explanation: In the Stage-Gate model, gates are checkpoint reviews where management evaluates the project's progress, feasibility, and alignment with strategy before approving the next stage.

questions.question: Which of the following correctly lists the five stages of Design Thinking?

options.text: Plan, Design, Build, Test, Launch
Empathise, Define, Ideate, Prototype, Test
Research, Strategy, Execution, Feedback, Scale
Discover, Define, Develop, Deliver, Deploy

questions.explanation: The Stanford d.school Design Thinking framework comprises five stages: Empathise (understand users), Define (frame the problem), Ideate (generate solutions), Prototype (build), and Test (validate).

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?

options.text: To launch the most feature-complete product possible from day one
To test the riskiest assumptions with the minimum effort and investment
To create a product with zero bugs before any customer testing
To generate maximum revenue in the first month

questions.explanation: An MVP is a product version with just enough features to test the most critical hypotheses and gather validated learning with minimum wasted effort.

questions.question: The 'Empathise' stage of Design Thinking primarily involves:

options.text: Writing technical specifications for the product
Understanding users' needs, experiences, and motivations deeply
Presenting the final product to investors
Setting the price for the product

questions.explanation: Empathising means understanding the human perspective by observing users, conducting interviews, and immersing oneself in the user experience to discover real needs.

questions.question: Which type of intellectual property protection is most appropriate for a unique software algorithm?

options.text: Trademark
Copyright alone (automatically applies to code)
Patent (if it meets novelty and non-obviousness criteria)
Trade dress

questions.explanation: A novel and non-obvious software algorithm may be patentable. While code is automatically copyrighted, patents provide broader protection for the underlying functional method.

questions.question: At which stage of new product development does concept screening primarily occur?

options.text: After full-scale manufacturing has begun
After idea generation, to evaluate which concepts merit further development
Only after the product has been sold to customers
During the advertising campaign planning stage

questions.explanation: Concept screening follows idea generation and uses criteria such as market potential, strategic fit, and technical feasibility to shortlist concepts worth investing in.

questions.question: A trademark primarily protects which element of a company's intellectual property?

options.text: The technical design of the product's internal mechanism
A brand name, logo, or slogan that distinguishes goods or services
The company's financial statements
The confidential source code of software

questions.explanation: A trademark protects brand identifiers — names, logos, slogans — that distinguish a company's goods or services from competitors, preventing consumer confusion.
